original_question: Which Banach spaces X have the property that the dual unit ball (B_{X*}, w*) is a semi-Eberlein compact space?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the unnumbered umbrella open problem in Section 7, stated immediately before Problem 7.4: “the main open problem here is clearly the one to characterise those Banach spaces whose dual ball is semi-Eberlein.” The numbered items in Problem 7.4 are then presented as narrower follow-up questions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right object—the weak* dual unit ball (B_{X*}, w*)—and asks for a characterization of the spaces X for which that compact space is semi-Eberlein. That matches the paper’s stated main open problem in Section 7, and it does not incorrectly narrow the question to WCG spaces, Asplund spaces, or spaces with a norming M-basis, which appear only in subsidiary questions such as Problem 7.4(1). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: The draft should define “semi-Eberlein” explicitly: a compact space K is semi-Eberlein iff it is homeomorphic to a compact subset of [-1,1]^Γ whose intersection with c0(Γ) is dense. This is Definition 7.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

It should spell out that B_{X*} means the closed unit ball of X* endowed with the weak* topology; this is the compact space embedded via the evaluation map in the Section 7 discussion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

To be fully stand-alone, it should explain c0(Γ) in the definition of semi-Eberlein, namely the scalar families on Γ that vanish at infinity. The paper leaves this as standard notation, but the stand-alone question should not. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

The draft does not indicate that, in the paper, this is the umbrella characterization problem, while Problem 7.4 records more specific special cases (for example, whether every Banach space with a norming M-basis has semi-Eberlein dual ball). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

The scalar-field convention is left implicit. The paper formulates semi-Eberlein compacta through embeddings into the real cube [-1,1]^Γ, so a paper-faithful stand-alone version should at least keep that real-cube formulation explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
refined_question: Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the weak* compact closed dual unit ball (B_{X*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein; equivalently, determine for which X there exist a set Γ and a homeomorphic embedding h:(B_{X*}, w*) → [-1,1]^Γ such that h(B_{X*}) ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in h(B_{X*}), where c0(Γ) denotes the scalar functions on Γ that vanish at infinity.
justification: Section 7 is the correct target because the paper first defines semi-Eberlein compacta in Definition 7.1, then turns specifically to semi-Eberlein dual balls. The surrounding context shows the two main sufficient mechanisms known in the paper: if X is a subspace of a WCG space, then (B_{X*}, w*) is Eberlein and hence semi-Eberlein (Section 3); and if X has a 1-norming M-basis, then Remark 7.3, using the norming criterion from Definition 2.1 and equation (2.1), yields that (B_{X*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein. Immediately after noting that these are essentially the only known sources of examples, the paper explicitly isolates the characterization of all Banach spaces with semi-Eberlein dual ball as the main open problem, and only afterward lists the narrower subquestions in Problem 7.4. Therefore the faithful refinement is the general characterization question, with the definition of semi-Eberlein made explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
